findings.evidence: compose-up.test.ts asserts that 'ports 3000 and 5432 refuse connections from the host'. But U1 publishes the dev database on 127.0.0.1:${JADE_DEV_DB_PORT:-5432}, and V5's env:init chooses 5432 whenever it is free. The per-bead gate (section 16 step 3) runs `pnpm test` (integration tests need that dev database), then `pnpm test:infra`, so the dev database is listening on 127.0.0.1:5432 when the infra test probes it. The connection succeeds and AC8 and `pnpm ci:local` fail on every machine where the dev database runs on the default port. This applies in every bugfix worktree too, since the primary checkout's database holds 5432.
findings.fix: Do not prove non-exposure by probing well-known host ports. Assert it from the stack itself: `docker compose -p <test project> port db 5432` and `port app 3000` return nothing; `docker inspect` shows empty published ports for the stack's db and app containers; the backend network is `internal: true`. Alternatively, probe only ports that the test first shows to be free. State the chosen check in INV7 and in the compose-up check list.
findings.path: plan.md section 11 Checks (tests/infra/compose-up.test.ts), section 9 U1, section 8 V5, section 16 step 3

findings.evidence: The runner takes a session advisory lock and then runs ensureAppRole(), which sets jade_app's password on every run. Advisory lock tags include the current database OID, so the lock only serializes runners on the same database. Roles, however, are cluster-wide. migrate.test.ts and db-scripts.test.ts each run migrate against their own scratch database, in parallel Vitest files on the same Postgres cluster. Two concurrent ALTER ROLE jade_app ... PASSWORD (or CREATE ROLE) statements on the same pg_authid row can fail with 'tuple concurrently updated' or 'role already exists'. The result is an intermittent integration failure that the plan's stop point ('same test failing three times') would then trip on.
findings.fix: Serialize the role bootstrap cluster-wide. Options: take the advisory lock for ensureAppRole in a fixed database such as `postgres`; skip ALTER ROLE when the stored verifier already matches; retry on SQLSTATE XX000/42710; or have the test global setup bootstrap the role once and run per-database migrations with role setup disabled. Add a check that runs two migrate() calls against two different databases at the same time.
findings.path: plan.md section 9 U2 and U3 steps 1-2; Checks (migrate.test.ts, db-scripts.test.ts)

findings.evidence: X4 says: apply the head's migrations to a fresh database, start the base build, then 'run the base's integration tests against that database'. But U7's harness never uses an existing database. The integration project's global setup migrates its own template from the checkout's own migrations/ directory, and createTestDatabase() clones that template. Run from the base checkout, the base's tests therefore run on the base schema, not the head's, so the job cannot catch a migration that breaks the previous app version. INV5 and OB53 count this job as a check, so the check is ineffective as designed, even though it first bites in Phase 2.
findings.fix: Specify a harness override that the base checkout honours, for example JADE_TEST_MIGRATIONS_DIR or JADE_TEST_TEMPLATE_DB. The base's global setup then builds its template by applying the head's migrations, or uses the template ci:compat prepared. Add an acceptance check to ci:compat that the template's ledger equals the head's manifest before the base's tests run. Note that this override must already exist in the harness at the base commit, so it has to be added in jade-urd now.
findings.path: plan.md section 12.1 X4; section 9 U7 (PD5); INV5; OB53 row

findings.evidence: INV1 says no log line written by the app contains a code, token, body, path or query string, and that any change to the line schema goes to Mike. A1 then adds a development-only path that prints the raw error, message and properties included, to the server's stdout. /dev/boom deliberately puts the query string in its message, and from Phase 2 a Postgres error's detail or parameters can carry a code or token from a demo-kit session. Rule 4 has no environment exemption ('never stored or logged'), and the brief requires no code, token or body in any log line. The carve-out is neither raised as a contradiction nor listed as a risk, and log-privacy.test.ts runs under APP_ENV=test, so nothing checks it.
findings.fix: Remove the raw-error print, and keep diagnosis through err_type, err_tag and stack_frames (RR6 already accepts that cost). Or raise it explicitly as a question for Mike (rule 4), with a residual-risk entry and a test that the print is unreachable unless APP_ENV=development.
findings.path: plan.md section 10 A1 ('In APP_ENV=development only, the raw error is also printed to the terminal'); INV1; CLAUDE.md rule 4

findings.evidence: The CI service-container password deliberately contains 'test-only', so any DATABASE_URL built from it is refused outside APP_ENV=test. route-access.test.ts boots the built server under APP_ENV=production, and Z5's banner e2e boots it under APP_ENV=staging. If either is given the job's database URL, as the e2e and blackbox helpers would naturally do, the server refuses to start in CI. The plan does not say what URL these non-test boots use.
findings.fix: In tests/support/server.ts, specify that a boot under staging or production gets a generated, non-marker dummy DATABASE_URL (the 404 and banner checks need no database) and generated secrets. Add that case to the helper's contract.
findings.path: plan.md section 8 V2 ('A value containing test-only is refused unless APP_ENV is test'); section 12.1 X2; section 10 route-access.test.ts; section 14 Z5

findings.evidence: Compose gives an exported COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME precedence over the file's top-level `name:`. The bugfix skill exports COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=bugfix-<bead>-<purpose> for each worktree. A manual `docker compose -f compose.prod.yml up` in such a shell would therefore join the dev project and recreate its `db` service with the prod definition, which falsifies the 'never touches' claim. The infra tests are safe because they pass -p.
findings.fix: Weaken the claim, or have the pnpm scripts that bring up the prod stack always pass an explicit -p. Also give the prod services and volumes names that cannot collide with the dev `db` service and its volume.
findings.path: plan.md section 11 D2 ('name: jade-stack ... bringing it up in a checkout never touches the development db service'); .claude/skills/bugfix/SKILL.md 'The gates'
